sentences.text:
11.12.2024 Order No. (Through hybrid mode)
05.

1. On 20.09.2024, time has been granted to the learned Additional Standing Counsel to go through the case diary in order to ascertain the whether the victim was suffering from physical or mental disability.
2. On 25.09.2024, the matter was adjourned on the prayer of the learned Additional Standing Counsel, Mr. J. P. Patra as he stated that he had not received instructions.

3. Today, Mr. U.C. Jena, learned Additional Standing Counsel brings to my notice the disability certificate which is available in the case diary which indicates that the victim is suffering from 40%
disability relating to delayed milestone, speech and locomotion.

4. This is the second application of the Petitioner under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. in connection with Kalimela P.S. Case No.210 of 2023 corresponding to C.T. Case No.165 of 2023 which is pending for trial in the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Malkanagiri punishable under section 376(2)(l)/376(2)(f)/376(2)(n) /506/342 of the IPC.
5. BLAPL No.12377 of 2023 filed earlier by the Petitioner has been rejected on 06.11.2023 granting liberty to the Petitioner to move for bail afresh after completion of investigation.
6. Charge sheet dated 23.10.2023 has been submitted against the Petitioner for commission of offence punishable under section 376(2)(l)/376(2)(n)/376(2)(f)/506/342 of the IPC.

7. Thereafter the prayer for bail of the Petitioner has been rejected by the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Malkanagiri on 03.04.2024.
8. Mr. P. K. Nanda, learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that the petitioner is in custody since August, 2023 and in the meanwhile, charge has been framed but trial has not commenced.

He also submits that false allegations have been made against the Petitioner as medical report regarding pregnancy of the victim do not support the allegations made in the FIR or the statement of the victim regarding date of occurrence.
9. Considering the nature of the allegations against the petitioner and the disability of the victim, I am not inclined to release the Petitioner on bail.
10. The BLAPL is accordingly dismissed.

11. It is open to the Petitioner to move for bail afresh in case there is undue delay in completion of the trial.
12.
Copy of this order be sent to the learned Trial Court by the Registry.
(Savitri Ratho) Judge Gitanjali Designation:
